summation.text: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) associated with the activated receptor for CSF1, CSF1R (M-CSFR), phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to yield phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3) (Saleem et al. 1995, also inferred from mouse homologs). The regulatory subunit of PI3K, PIK3R1 (p85alpha), binds phosphotyrosine-723 (721 in the mouse homologs) of CSF1R (inferred from mouse homologs). PI3K is important for proliferation, migration, and anti-inflammatory activity of macrophages (inferred from mouse homologs).
